books.section: Topic 7.7 1920s: Innovations in Communication and Technology

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.7: In 1927, record producer Ralph Peer traveled through the South to record local string bands, balladeers, and other musicians in gospel, blues, and ragtime. Sessions held in Bristol, Tennessee, launched nationally known country performers Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family. Record companies had begun issuing “hillbilly” records in 1923 and 1924.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.7.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.7
stem: The Bristol sessions best show that new recording technology

options.text: erased all regional differences in music
options.misconception: The sessions spread regional music; they did not erase it. Country music kept its Southern sound as it went national.

options.text: was used only for classical music performances
options.misconception: Peer recorded string bands, balladeers, gospel, and blues, not only classical music. Popular and folk music were the point.

options.text: carried local music to a national audience
ended live performance across the South
options.misconception: Recording did not end live performance. Rodgers and the Carter Family toured and performed live after Bristol.

rationales.A: The sessions spread regional music; they did not erase it. Country music kept its Southern sound as it went national.
rationales.B: Peer recorded string bands, balladeers, gospel, and blues, not only classical music. Popular and folk music were the point.
rationales.C: Peer's recordings took Southern string bands and singers to listeners across the country. Local music became national music.
rationales.D: Recording did not end live performance. Rodgers and the Carter Family toured and performed live after Bristol.
rationales.general:
1. Note what Peer did: he traveled south to record local musicians in place.
2. Note what happened next: Rodgers and the Carter Family became known across the country.
3. Name the role of the technology: recording carried local sounds outward to a national audience.
Remember: recording is a carrier, so ask what it carried and how far it went.
